title: Automatic subscription redress can reduce claim burden while receipt and correction remain unobserved
source_unit: Eligible Amazon Prime consumers in the FTC/Amazon redress program; aggregate program payments

denominator.unit: Eligible Prime consumers; the official September 2026 update describes millions of additional eligible consumers but does not give a usable program denominator for issued or accepted payments.

redress_issued_by_september_2026.unit: dollars in redress payments Amazon had issued to eligible consumers by September 2026

maximum_total_payment.unit: dollars per eligible consumer under the revised settlement order

automatic_payment_channels.unit: officially stated automatic payment channels; no claim form, notice response, or additional paperwork is required for future automatic payments

observations.method: FTC September 2026 settlement update describes Amazon's aggregate redress issuance, revised eligibility, automatic distribution design, payment channels, and scheduled future payment stages. The source is an administrative program update, not a consumer follow-up survey or account-level payment file.
observations.uncertainty: The $845 million figure is aggregate amount issued, not a count of consumers paid, accepted payments, net losses corrected, or benefit received. The number and characteristics of eligible, reached, paid, and accepting consumers are not provided in a common denominator. Future payment stages remained scheduled at the update date.
observations.subgroup: Eligible Prime consumers affected by the challenged enrollment or cancellation flows; later eligibility expands to consumers who used 11–20 Prime benefits in a year. Individual exposure, need, payment acceptance, and subscription status are not reported.
observations.counterinterpretation: Automatic payment removes some claim-form and notice-response burden, but it does not demonstrate that a consumer received, accepted, or could use the payment; nor does it establish correction of enrollment/cancellation, restored control, continued use, switching, non-use, trust, or household recovery.

related_sources.claim: FTC consumer-facing program page describes eligibility, automatic payment channels, payment expiration, and the April 2027 completion schedule.

boundary: This record adds an aggregate redress-issuance and low-burden distribution stage after a named subscription practice. It does not show individual receipt, acceptance, account correction, subscription cancellation, continued use, switching, trust, or household recovery; issued redress must not be read as completed remedy.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: SHA-256 is of the official FTC press-release HTML retrieved on 2026-09-24. No customer data, payment file, or claim-level data was acquired.
